title: COUNT, SUM, and grouping

spans.text: “COUNT, SUM, and grouping” is a tool for solving a concrete programming problem. Identify the input and desired result, then trace what role the construct plays in the example. Study it not only as syntax, but also for its effects on readability, correctness, resource use, and future changes.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.

spans.code:
SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS learners,
       AVG(score) AS average_score
FROM enrollments
GROUP BY course_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

spans.text: Shows enrollment count and average score for courses with at least two enrollments.

COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX summarize multiple rows. GROUP BY forms groups; HAVING filters groups after aggregation, while WHERE filters rows before grouping. COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) ignores NULL values in that column.

Key line: `SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS learners,`
What it does: Shows enrollment count and average score for courses with at least two enrollments.
Why it is used: Use WHERE for row conditions and HAVING for conditions on aggregate results.
If omitted or changed: Most aggregates ignore NULL values; understand empty groups and the distinction from COUNT(*).

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: Mixing aggregates and ordinary columns without a valid GROUP BY can fail or produce ambiguous results.
